title: Higher Education Support Legislation Amendment (2016 Measures No. 1) Bill 2016
short_title: Higher Education Support Legislation Amendment (2016 Measures No. 1) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would create a new grant program for universities to support Indigenous students.
It would also let the Departmental Secretary receive Tax File Numbers to manage student debts under the VET FEE-HELP scheme.
The bill would authorise Commonwealth officers to use and disclose Tax File Numbers for administering HELP debts.
changes: Inserts a new part into the Higher Education Support Act 2003 for grants to help Indigenous students.
Allows the Secretary to obtain Tax File Numbers for VET FEE-HELP administration.
Authorises use and disclosure of Tax File Numbers for future HELP program administration.
summary.affected: Universities, higher education providers, Indigenous students, and the Departmental Secretary.

speeches.speaker: Karen Andrews
speeches.brief: The bill consolidates existing Indigenous student support programs into a single part of the Higher Education Support Act 2003, with new guidelines to be issued by Minister Scullion, and amends tax file number collection for VET FEE-HELP to improve data management and protect students from unethical providers.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: The opposition supported the bill, which pools three Indigenous higher education grant funds into one flexible fund and allows tax file number sharing for VET FEE-HELP debtors. It also criticised government higher education funding cuts, including a proposed $152 million reduction to the Higher Education Participation and Partnerships Program.

speeches.speaker: Melissa Price
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Higher Education Support Legislation Amendment (2016 Measures No. 1) Bill 2016 would streamline Indigenous student support by consolidating programs under simpler guidelines and collecting tax file numbers for VET FEE-HELP, aiming to boost Indigenous university completion rates and employment prospects. The bill merges the Commonwealth Scholarships Program, Indigenous Support Program, and Indigenous Tutorial Assistance Scheme, with funding distributed based on enrolment, progression, and completion rates.

speeches.speaker: Julian Hill
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill's consolidation of Indigenous student support programs and technical data-sharing amendments, but criticised the government for lacking broader education reform and highlighted poor completion rates and failures in vocational education.

speeches.speaker: Justine Elliot
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Higher Education Support Legislation Amendment Bill 2016, which consolidates three Indigenous student funding sources into the Indigenous Student Success Program and allows tax file number access for VET FEE-HELP debtors, but criticised the government for cutting education funding, citing $29 billion in school cuts and plans for $100,000 university degrees, while contrasting Labor’s record of a 70% increase in Indigenous student participation and a proposed $13 billion higher education investment.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill, which streamlines grants for Indigenous university students and improves data sharing for VET FEE-HELP loans. They noted a 50% increase in Indigenous university enrolments since 2009 and highlighted the University of New South Wales’ Nura Gili program and Matraville Education Partnership, which improved NAPLAN results and year 12 completions, while criticising the government for mismanaging VET FEE-HELP and cutting $2.5 billion from skills training.

speeches.speaker: Steve Georganas
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill to pool three separate Indigenous student support funds into one to reduce administrative burden, and argued Labor has a strong record on higher education, citing 190,000 more students, a 26% boost in Indigenous student numbers, and a 30% increase in regional students under their government.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The bill creates the Indigenous Students Success Program to improve university graduation rates for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, and allows the Department of Education and Training to collect tax file numbers for VET FEE-HELP and HELP loan administration.
